claims.text: The proposed workflow replaces explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics free-energy evaluation with an actively learned moment tensor potential trained on finite-temperature ab initio configurations.
An analytical entropy-correction scheme is included to account for vibrational and anharmonic effects.
The AL-MTP workflow will accurately capture vibrational contributions to free energies.
The AL-MTP workflow will accurately capture anharmonic free-energy contributions.
The workflow will capture or approximate electron-vibration coupling effects.
The workflow will retain the relevant free-energy contributions in both solid and liquid phases.
An actively learned MTP can represent an ab initio-derived potential-energy surface in multicomponent alloys.
Active-learning interpolation avoids the need to sample an enormous configurational space.
The analytical entropy correction compensates for residual free-energy contributions critical to the phase transition.
Vibrational entropy can contribute to the thermodynamic stabilization of high-entropy alloy structures.
The method is intended for elemental, binary, and multicomponent high-entropy alloys near their melting points.
The proposed temperature domain is approximately 0.8 to 1.2 times the fusion temperature.
Fusion temperature, latent heat, and solid-liquid free-energy differences will agree within approximately 10% of explicit AIMD results.
The workflow will reduce computational cost by roughly one order of magnitude relative to explicit AIMD.
The workflow will scale better than TOR-TILD for multicomponent systems.
The method is expected to remain valid up to high-entropy-alloy compositional complexity when vibrational and anharmonic entropy dominate near melting.
Transferability in systems with extreme electron-vibration coupling or very high anharmonicity is uncertain.
A deviation greater than 10% from AIMD fusion properties or a cost reduction smaller than tenfold would falsify the hypothesis.
